correctness.rationale: Fixedness gives y=0 and x+f_mu(x)=0 modulo one; the latter lift has derivative (1-mu²)/(1-2mu cos(2πx-alpha)+mu²)>0 and degree one. At x=arcsin(mu)/π the arctangent equals -arcsin(mu) and f'_mu=0. The two-step equations follow from y'=x'-x; the seed Jacobian has determinant 5, giving analytic continuation with primitive, disjoint cycles. Writing c=cos(2πa_0), the first displacement of both first coordinates is c mu/π. Substitution directly into the rational derivative gives d_a=2mu sin(2πa_0)+2(1-c)mu²+O(mu³) and d_b with the opposite linear term. The exact trace 7+3(d_a+d_b)+d_a d_b therefore has coefficient 8-12c+4c², which gives (25-7√5)/2 and (25+7√5)/2 in the stated order. This verifies the Finding analytically, without relying on the supplied Newton examples. For the last step differentiate the conjugacy equation for the second iterate once (rather than twice as worded in the proof); a C¹ diffeomorphic conjugacy preserves the two-step traces. The asymptotics and obstruction are local in mu.
